title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Develop and Present an Economic Policy Proposal
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: shortened the longest-key choice in q1, added the round-only-at-the-final-step instruction to q3, corrected the q3 explanation of the subtract-5%-per-year error. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: Which sentence states the mechanism of a policy proposal?

choices.text: A repair fund cuts the time students lose fetching water, which lowers the opportunity cost of school.
The proposal will serve about 1,100 students in four rural schools in the eastern part of District K.
The repair fund will cost about $41,000 per year and will be paid for from the town's general budget.
Attendance at the four schools should rise from 85% to 90% within two school years of the launch.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A town plans to pay for a school water-repair fund by moving money out of its public library budget. What should the proposal say about the cost of this funding choice?

choices.text: The plan costs the town nothing, because it uses money that is already in the town's budget.
The plan's cost should be counted twice, once for the library and once for the new repair fund.
The plan's opportunity cost is the library services that the moved money would have paid for.
The plan involves no trade-off, as long as the total size of the town's budget stays the same.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A proposal includes a $22,050 equipment replacement that will be paid two years from now. Using a discount rate of 5% per year, what is the present value of that cost, in dollars? Round only at the final step. (Enter a number only.)
Which indicator statement is complete enough to measure the progress of a proposal?

choices.text: Improve access to safe drinking water at the schools as much as possible over time, using the best data.
Share of school days with working drinking water: from 65% in 2026 to 90% by 2028, from maintenance logs.
The share of school days with working drinking water should rise a lot, as teachers notice over the year.
By 2028 students will be healthier and happier at school, as shown by a survey that we may run later on.

questions.prompt: Which sentence from a capstone reflection best names a real limitation and a next step?

choices.text: I worked very hard on this project, and I think my proposal is excellent, so I would keep it as it is.
My proposal is strong, but the rubric was unfair to me, because it asked for far too much evidence.
I learned a lot about water. Next time I would choose a different SDG so that the project is easier.
My effect estimate came from before-and-after data alone, so next time I would look for a comparison group.
